message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep completed for the monitored product list in Products.txt, covering the last 24 hours ending with this scheduled run. I found one credible, clearly product-matched vulnerability newly published in the window: Grafana Operator CVE-2026-11769. I also found several fresh WordPress plugin advisories that are related to the WordPress ecosystem but are not confirmed matches to the named WordPress, Yoast SEO, or Advanced Custom Fields products in the monitored list.

**Finding 1: Grafana Operator path traversal / privilege escalation**

- Product: Grafana Operator
- Issue: CVE-2026-11769
- Severity: Moderate in the CVE/GitHub Advisory scoring, with CVSS v4 score 6.4; the advisory text also describes the underlying fix as critical severity.
- Description: Grafana Operator versions up to and including 5.23 can evaluate Jsonnet-based Dashboard or LibraryPanel resources in the operator manager pod context. A malicious user able to create those resources could obtain the Kubernetes service account token for the Grafana Operator manager.
- Why it appears relevant: The monitored list includes Grafana, and this issue affects Grafana Operator, an official Grafana ecosystem component used to manage Grafana in Kubernetes.
- Sources: CVE.org https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-11769; GitHub Advisory Database https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v82c-5c2q-hx9g

**Possible matches needing review**

- Product family: WordPress plugins
- Issues: Fresh advisories were published for multiple WordPress plugins, including Bookly CVE-2026-5513, WP Ticket CVE-2026-9848, GPTranslate CVE-2026-9109, Meow Gallery CVE-2026-1291, Pagelayer CVE-2026-2470 and CVE-2026-3297, Canvas CVE-2026-9629, FooGallery CVE-2026-9134, Store Locator CVE-2026-9061 and CVE-2026-9062, and LWS Optimize CVE-2026-12089. Reported severities range from unknown/moderate to high.
- Why review is needed: The monitored list includes WordPress plus specific plugins Yoast SEO and Advanced Custom Fields. These advisories are for other WordPress plugins, so they are relevant only if any of those plugins are installed in the monitored WordPress environments. I did not treat them as confirmed findings because the named affected plugins do not match the product list directly.
- Sources: Wordfence vulnerability database https://www.wordfence.com/threat-intel/vulnerabilities; GitHub Advisory Database https://github.com/advisories?query=sort%3Aupdated-desc

No other credible new vulnerability reports were confirmed in the last 24 hours for the remaining monitored products. MongoDB, Ubiquiti/UniFi, Cisco, Chrome/Edge, Microsoft, Ubuntu, OpenSSL, Fortinet, SonicWall, VMware, and related results seen during the sweep were excluded when their primary disclosure or vendor publication fell outside the freshness window or did not cleanly match the monitored product scope.

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for any Kubernetes deployments using Grafana Operator 5.23 or earlier. The WordPress items should be checked against the actual plugin inventory before treating them as actionable exposure.
